title: Variables
summary: Variables store values so you can reuse, modify, or reference them later in your program. They act like labeled containers that hold data.
sample_question: What is a variable and why is it useful?

title: Loops
summary: Loops let you repeat an action multiple times without writing the same line of code again. Common loops include 'for' and 'while'.
sample_question: Explain the difference between a for loop and a while loop.

title: Functions
summary: Functions let you group code into reusable blocks. They help organize logic, avoid repetition, and make programs easier to maintain.
sample_question: Why do we use functions in programming?

title: Conditionals
summary: Conditionals allow your program to make decisions using if/else statements. They let code run only when certain conditions are met.
sample_question: What is the purpose of an if-else statement?

title: Arrays
summary: Arrays store multiple values in a single container, accessed by index. They're useful for lists of related items.
sample_question: What is an array and how do you access an element in it?

title: Objects
summary: Objects represent real-world things using properties and behaviors. They allow structured, organized data and form the basis of OOP.
sample_question: What makes objects useful in object-oriented programming?

title: Classes
summary: Classes act like blueprints for creating objects. They define the shape and behavior that all objects of that type will have.
sample_question: What is a class and how is it related to objects?

title: Recursion
summary: Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller part of a problem. It is often used for problems with repeated substructure.
sample_question: Explain recursion in simple terms and give an example.

title: Data Structures
summary: Data structures like stacks, queues, and trees store data in specific ways that improve performance and organization.
sample_question: What is a data structure and why do we need different types?

title: Algorithms
summary: Algorithms are step-by-step procedures for solving problems. Good algorithms are efficient, clear, and reliable.
sample_question: What is an algorithm? Explain with a simple example.

title: Big O Notation
summary: Big O notation describes how the runtime or space usage of an algorithm grows as the input size increases.
sample_question: What does Big O measure and why is it important?

title: APIs
summary: APIs allow different software systems to communicate. They define how data is requested, sent, and processed between applications.
sample_question: What is an API and why do developers use them?
